verdict_explanation: There is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE to classify any South Mumbai area as experiencing gentrification or displacement. While official RBI transaction records confirm strong city-level housing price appreciation over 15 years (+370.39%), empirical data on localized ward-level prices, demographic turnover, tenant displacement, and construction permits is unavailable from official free sources. In accordance with academic integrity standards, UrbanLens does not assign automated gentrification labels.

pillars.name: Housing Market Dynamics & Price Trajectory
key_findings: Recent market regime: Plateau & Valuation Consolidation.
limitations: Official transaction assessment index at metropolitan city scale.
Ward-level residential price disaggregation is unavailable from official free sources.
pillars.hypothesis_interpretation: Official RBI transaction records verify sustained long-term capital appreciation in Mumbai. However, price growth alone is a macroeconomic phenomenon and does NOT demonstrate localized gentrification.

pillars.name: Demographic & Socioeconomic Composition Shifts
key_findings: Official Census 2021 municipal ward enumeration tables remain unreleased by the Government of India.
2011 Census tables are 15 years old and cannot establish contemporary population turnover.
No official ward-level income or wealth distribution surveys exist.
limitations: Ethical standards forbid fabricating synthetic demographics to simulate gentrification.
pillars.hypothesis_interpretation: Without empirical demographic data on household income, education levels, and in-migration, it is scientifically impossible to confirm gentrification in South Mumbai.

pillars.name: Infrastructure & Civic Amenities
key_findings: 232 verified real civic nodes mapped in South Mumbai (hospitals, clinics, schools, transit, parking).
limitations: Historical infrastructure expansion velocity is NOT measurable from a single snapshot.
pillars.hypothesis_interpretation: South Mumbai possesses high civic infrastructure density as an established urban core. However, present-day amenity presence cannot be conflated with recent gentrification investment.

pillars.name: Land-Use & Redevelopment Activity
key_findings: MCGM building permit approvals (IOD/CC) are not published via open machine-readable REST APIs.
SRA slum rehabilitation GIS boundary layers are unavailable in public georeferenced formats.
limitations: Physical redevelopment activity cannot be quantified without municipal permit registers.
pillars.hypothesis_interpretation: Empirical construction velocity data is unavailable.

pillars.name: Housing Affordability & Displacement Pressure
key_findings: No official residential rental index exists in India.
Eviction court records and tenancy tenure changes are not accessible in structured formats.
limitations: Displacement pressure cannot be claimed without longitudinal rent and tenant tenure records.
pillars.hypothesis_interpretation: Gentrification by definition requires evidence of demographic displacement and housing cost burden. UrbanLens strictly refuses to assign arbitrary displacement risk scores without empirical evidence.

academic_mandate: Urban transformation is a multi-dimensional socioeconomic process. UrbanLens refuses to equate macroeconomic housing price appreciation with gentrification.
